note: Week 1, full budget for everyone leaguewide (no bids cleared yet) — pricing is band-only, not owner-history-calibrated for this specific market. No PURSUE targets this run: fresh research corrects two of the Sept 11 brief's premises (see below), and the honest read on a deep 15-man bench is that nothing on the wire clears the bar to cut a rostered piece.

targets.why: Came out of retirement to sign with Carolina, ran with the Panthers' first-team offense in practice, and is described by beat reporting (Panthers.com, Washington Post, mid-to-late Aug) as the team's top red-zone and third-down tight end weapon ahead of his first regular-season game back since Miami in 2025 (24 catches, 283 yds, 6 TD in 9 games there).
targets.asset: role-based -- red-zone/third-down usage reported from camp; zero regular-season snaps in this stint yet
targets.my_team_impact: Would not crack the starting lineup over Sam LaPorta. Jake Ferguson, my current TE2, is Dallas' locked TE1 (82 catches, 8 TDs last year) with no lost snaps reported, so there's no real drop candidate to open this add -- it would mean carrying a 3rd TE, which only pays off on a Ferguson bye or injury.
targets.confidence_why: Role is described in camp/practice terms, not yet a single confirmed regular-season snap, on a 33-year-old two-year-removed-from-retirement body.
targets.competition: DadKing rosters only Kyle Pitts at TE and is the one team with a plausible thin spot at the position; no one else shows an acute TE hole this week.
targets.bid: 2-4 dollars if you want the speculative stash; not worth pushing further
targets.drop: No clean drop -- Ferguson holds real TE1 value in Dallas. Only worth adding if you're willing to carry a 3rd TE over a rostered RB/WR piece, which isn't recommended this week.

targets.why: CORRECTION to the Sept 11 brief, which called him the Raiders' 'presumptive Week 1 WR1.' Fresh Week 1 outlook reporting (FantasyPros, SI.com) instead has Tucker projected for a ~15% target share in a three-way split with Jalen Nailor (14%) and Jack Bech (13%), with Brock Bowers still the clear passing-game leader (25% target share) and analysts openly cautious about starting Tucker in Week 1.
targets.asset: projection (preseason) -- part of a genuine three-way WR2/3/4 competition, not a clear WR1 as previously reported
targets.my_team_impact: Downgraded from yesterday's PURSUE. The Sept 11 brief's drop candidate, Quentin Johnston, also needs correcting: Keenan Allen left the Chargers in free agency, and fresh reporting has Johnston drawing a real ~20% target share in new OC Mike McDaniel's vertical scheme (plus a 65-yard preseason TD) -- he is a keep, not a scoopable bench piece. With no clean drop candidate, Tucker isn't worth the roster spot this week.
targets.confidence_why: Role read materially softened between Sept 11 and Sept 12 reporting -- a three-way split is a real signal against confident Week 1 volume for any one of the three.
targets.competition: No HBGBs roster currently holds a Raiders receiver or ties to this backfield/passing-game need.
targets.bid: n/a -- pass this week; revisit once Week 1 snaps/targets settle the three-way split
targets.drop: n/a -- Quentin Johnston is no longer a recommended drop (see correction above).

targets.why: San Francisco's receiver room is down two bodies behind Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel after Christian Kirk's IR stint and Ricky Pearsall's season-ending surgery, with De'Zhaun Stribling's Sept 10 ankle injury (nfl-events.json) trimming it further -- Robinson is a depth beneficiary by process of elimination.
targets.asset: role-based -- WR3/4 in a thinned SF receiver room; no confirmed regular-season target share yet
targets.my_team_impact: You don't roster a 49ers pass-catcher, and your own bench WRs (Odunze, Boutte, Johnston) already carry clearer, more established target shares than a fourth option in San Francisco's rotation.
targets.confidence_why: Depth-chart-math case, not a role report -- SF's WR3/4 job hasn't been named by the coaching staff.
targets.competition: Evans is StoneBone69's and Samuel is ENOTS's, so two rivals are exposed to this offense but not specifically needy for a WR add here.

targets.why: 49ers' confirmed RB2 behind a 30-year-old Christian McCaffrey, 197K Sleeper adds this week (the single most-added player leaguewide) on strong preseason usage (7.0 YPC vs. Las Vegas).
targets.my_team_impact: You don't roster McCaffrey, so this is a pure speculative stash with no direct payoff on your roster, and your RB room (Taylor/Jeanty/Irving/Tuten/Washington) is already five deep with no open bench math for a zero-touch handcuff.
targets.confidence_why: Handcuff value only matters to McCaffrey's own roster (Sladsous) -- doesn't transfer to yours regardless of leaguewide add volume.
targets.competition: Likely to clear a real bid from Sladsous or another McCaffrey-adjacent roster; not a competitive question for your team.

targets.why: Named Atlanta's Week 1 starter over Michael Penix Jr. after Tua Tagovailoa's Thursday oblique injury (nfl-events.json, Sept 11).
targets.asset: role-based -- one-week (at least) starting job on a backup-caliber arm
targets.my_team_impact: No fit -- Justin Herbert is a clear locked starter, and this format's shallow one-QB math doesn't reward carrying a streamer when your starter isn't in question.
targets.confidence_why: Role is confirmed for at least this week, but there's no scenario where it matters to a roster that already has a clear starting QB.
targets.competition: No rival is QB-needy this early.
